name: Lawn

composition.value: Usually cotton (combed or carded yarn); historically linen

cotton_percentage.value: Typically 100% cotton for cotton lawn; blended or linen versions exist

gsm.value: About 50-100 GSM in trade listings (e.g. one Lahore supplier lists printed cotton lawn at 60 GSM); individual specs, not an industry standard

construction.value: Plain weave from fine, high-count yarns; thread count roughly 150-200 cited

texture.value: Smooth and silky with a crisp hand: crisper than voile, softer than organza/organdy

surface.value: Flat and even with no surface texture; semi-sheer, ranging from gauzy to near-opaque

breathability.value: High: fine open plain weave suited to hot weather

drape.value: Light, soft-to-semi-crisp drape depending on finish; never fully stiff

seasons.value: Spring and summer; Pakistani lawn collections launch around February

printing.value: Excellent; South Asian lawn is almost always bleached and then printed. [Method, estimate: reactive and digital printing are the usual cotton routes]

embroidery.value: Good; widely embroidered (necklines, borders, dupatta panels) in Pakistani lawn suits, though very fine lawn may need stabiliser

dyeing.value: Takes dye well; may be piece-dyed and then printed

garments.value: Dresses, blouses, shirts, nightwear, handkerchiefs, lingerie; 3-piece unstitched lawn suits (shirt, dupatta, trouser) in Pakistan

care.value: Machine or hand wash; Sewport lists medium-to-hot washing for the fibre, but printed suits are better washed cool and dried in shade to protect colour; iron while slightly damp

advantages: Very breathable and cool in heat
limitations: Semi-sheer; lighter lawn often needs lining
Colours of printed lawn can fade with sun and hot washing
notes: Lawn is the flagship summer fabric of the Pakistani market: brands release printed 2- and 3-piece unstitched lawn collections each year from around February. Pakistan and India are now the main producers. Combed lawn costs more than carded lawn.

name: Cotton

composition.value: Natural cellulose fibre from the cotton plant

gsm.value: Varies widely by construction: sheer voile/lawn sit at the light end, denim and canvas at the heavy end. There is no single GSM for 'cotton'

construction.value: Any: woven (plain, twill, satin) or knit (jersey, interlock, fleece)

weight_class.value: Light to heavy depending on construction

texture.value: Soft and comfortable; hand depends on yarn and finish

breathability.value: High: natural fibre that absorbs moisture

drape.value: Medium; varies with weight and weave

seasons.value: All seasons depending on weight; light cottons for summer

printing.value: Not suited to sublimation: disperse dye does not bond to cotton and washes out. [Estimate: reactive (screen/rotary/digital) and pigment printing are the standard cotton methods]

embroidery.value: Very good on medium and stable weaves

dyeing.value: Reactive, vat and direct dyes; dyes evenly

garments.value: T-shirts, shirts, underwear, casualwear, shalwar kameez, bedding

care.value: Machine washable; may shrink unless pre-shrunk; can wrinkle

limitations: Can fade with repeated hot washes
notes: In Pakistan, 'cotton' on a suit label is often a generic tag for medium-weight plain-woven cotton; lawn, cambric, poplin, voile and khaddar are all cotton fabrics that differ by yarn and construction.

drape.value: Crisp and structured rather than fluid
